ncc3abcf9fdf.s: Which of the following was cited as a reason for rejecting proportional representation for Lok Sabha elections?
o: It guarantees direct election in every single-member constituency
It may lead to unstable governments
It reduces the cost of elections
ncc3abcf9fdf.x: Unstable governments, fragmentation, expense, difficulty for voters and a weaker voter–MP link were cited against PR; guaranteeing direct election in single-member seats is not such a reason.

nindian-polity-36-9.s: Which of the following has no role in the election of the Vice-President of India?
nindian-polity-36-9.x: The Vice-President is elected only by MPs of both Houses, elected and nominated; State Legislatures have no role.

nc05ce523862.s: The Delimitation Commission of 1973 was chaired by:
nc05ce523862.x: Justice J.L. Kapur chaired the 1973 Commission; Justice Kuldip Singh chaired the 2002 Commission.

nindian-polity-38-18.s: Delimitation redraws territorial constituency boundaries on the basis of:
nindian-polity-38-18.x: Delimitation uses recent census figures so that each seat has roughly equal population, ensuring equal representation.

n770e12ae54d.s: Under Article 329, an election can be challenged only by:
o: A reference to the Election Commission
n770e12ae54d.x: Article 329 bars courts in electoral matters; an election can be questioned only through an election petition.

na36bcd3e362.s: Which of the following is a category of observer appointed by the Election Commission under Section 20B?
na36bcd3e362.x: Section 20B observers are general, police and expenditure observers; there is no judicial observer.

nf546ff8f15e.s: Trial of election petitions by the High Court is provided in which Section of the RPA, 1951?
nf546ff8f15e.x: Section 80A provides for trial by the High Court; Section 81 prescribes the 45-day filing limit.

nindian-polity-36-5.s: Disputes relating to the election of the President and Vice-President are decided by the:
nindian-polity-36-5.x: Under Article 71, Presidential and Vice-Presidential election disputes go to the Supreme Court, not the ECI.

nindian-polity-53-3.s: Under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951, political parties are registered by the:
nindian-polity-53-3.x: Section 29A of the RPA, 1951 empowers the Election Commission of India to register political parties.

n3cb4d1ee4de.s: The Dinesh Goswami Committee on electoral reforms was set up in:
n3cb4d1ee4de.x: The Goswami Committee dates from 1990; 1993 is the Vohra Committee on the crime-politics nexus.

nindian-polity-53-27.s: Which of the following was recommended by the Dinesh Goswami Committee?
o: Allocation of State Legislative Council seats
A selection panel of PM, LoP and CJI
nindian-polity-53-27.x: The Goswami Committee recommended EVMs and State funding, leading to the 1996 RPA amendment; Council seat allocation was not its subject.

nindian-polity-25-13.s: Under Section 33(7) of the RPA, 1951, a candidate can contest a Lok Sabha or Assembly election from at most:
nindian-polity-25-13.x: Section 33(7), added in 1996, limits a candidate to two constituencies.

n24d2424602b.s: The Kovind High-Level Committee recommended that, after simultaneous Lok Sabha and Assembly polls, local-body elections be held within:
n24d2424602b.x: The committee recommended Lok Sabha and Assembly polls together first, followed by local-body elections within 100 days.

n23e870ce7e5.s: Disclosure of criminal antecedents of candidates is dealt with in which Section of the RPA, 1951?
n23e870ce7e5.x: Section 33A concerns disclosure of criminal antecedents; Section 8 is disqualification, 29A registration and 123 corrupt practices.

nc255b81140e.s: Which Section of the RPA, 1951 requires a candidate to keep an account of election expenses?
nc255b81140e.x: Section 77 requires the account to be kept; Section 78 requires it to be filed with the DEO within 30 days.

nindian-polity-53-24.s: The 1996 cap on contesting from more than two constituencies followed the 1991 election in which ____ contested from three Lok Sabha seats.
nindian-polity-53-24.x: The 1996 amendment capped contests at two constituencies after Devi Lal stood from three Lok Sabha seats in 1991.

n5ecf91fa256.s: In ADR v ECI (2024), on the demand to return to paper ballots, the Supreme Court:
o: Ordered a return to paper ballots
Refused to order a return to paper ballots
n5ecf91fa256.x: The Supreme Court refused to order a return to paper ballots and has repeatedly upheld the use of EVMs.

n58f4a1deed3.s: NOTA was first used in a Lok Sabha election in:
n58f4a1deed3.x: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly elections; its first Lok Sabha use was in 2014.

na6e02e56268.s: How many special courts have been set up for criminal cases involving MPs and MLAs?
na6e02e56268.x: 12 special courts have been set up for MP/MLA cases, while a PIL seeking a lifetime ban on convicted legislators is pending.

nc48fc61af63.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about electoral bonds?
o: They were sold only by the State Bank of India
They were issued in denominations from ₹1,000 to ₹10 crore
nc48fc61af63.x: The denominations ran from ₹1,000 to ₹1 crore, not ₹10 crore; SBI was the only seller and the bearer bonds were valid for 15 days.

n7bcae15640f.s: Article 356, named among the provisions in the simultaneous-elections debate, deals with:
o: Appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner
n7bcae15640f.x: Article 356 concerns President's Rule; Article 83 is duration of Houses of Parliament and Article 174 dissolution of State Legislatures.

n0f0e7e9ea5e.s: The AIADMK split from the DMK after the death of:
n0f0e7e9ea5e.x: The AIADMK broke away after the death of C.N. Annadurai, not Karunanidhi.

n0d4af91705a.s: Political parties entered the Constitution through the Tenth Schedule, inserted by the:
n0d4af91705a.x: Parties were not in the original Constitution; they entered it via the Tenth Schedule added by the 52nd Amendment in 1985.

n765043e1ef0.s: In INC v Institute of Social Welfare (2002), the Supreme Court held that the Election Commission:
o: Can deregister any party for non-compliance
Cannot ordinarily deregister a political party
Can deregister a party for not contesting elections
n765043e1ef0.x: The ECI cannot deregister a party except in cases of fraud or where the party is declared unlawful.

nceb91d65734.s: Political parties must disclose every year the donors who give more than:
nceb91d65734.x: Donors above ₹20,000 are disclosed annually; ₹2,000 is the cap above which donations must be by cheque or bank transfer.

nindian-polity-54-18.s: The All India Trinamool Congress was formed in:
nindian-polity-54-18.x: The TMC was formed in 1998; the SP dates from 1992, the NCP from 1999 and the BSP from 1984.

new.s: The first use of an Electronic Voting Machine in India, in 1982, was in:
new.x: EVMs were first used at Parur in Kerala in 1982; Noksen saw the first VVPAT in 2013.

new.s: VVPAT was first used in 2013 at:
new.x: The first VVPAT use was at Noksen, Nagaland, in 2013.

new.s: In N. Chandrababu Naidu v Union of India (2019), VVPAT slips were to be tallied in how many polling stations per Assembly segment?
new.x: The 2019 ruling raised the VVPAT tally from one to five polling stations per Assembly segment.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about ADR v ECI (2024):
1. The Supreme Court rejected 100% VVPAT slip counting.
2. Second- and third-placed candidates may seek checks of 5% of EVMs per constituency.
3. Such a request must be made within 30 days of the results.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the written request must be made within 7 days of results, not 30.

new.s: Redrawing of constituency boundaries on the 2001 Census, with total seats unchanged, was provided by the:
new.x: The 87th Amendment (2003) allowed boundary redrawing on the 2001 Census without changing total seats.

new.s: Which of the following Amendment – delimitation effect pairs is correctly matched?
o: 84th Amendment – Boundaries redrawn on the 2001 Census
42nd Amendment – Freeze of State seat shares on the 1971 Census
87th Amendment – Freeze till the first census after 2026
new.x: The 42nd Amendment froze seat shares on the 1971 Census; the 84th extended the freeze till after 2026 and the 87th used the 2001 Census for boundaries.

new.s: Which of the following is an ex officio member of the Delimitation Commission under the 2002 Act?
o: The State Election Commissioner of the State concerned
The Governor of the State concerned
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chief Minister of the State concerned
new.x: Members are a Supreme Court judge (Chairperson), the CEC or an EC nominated by him, and the State Election Commissioner concerned, ex officio.

new.s: The constitutional ceiling of 550 elected Lok Sabha seats is made up of:
new.x: The ceiling is 550 (530 States + 20 UTs); the old 552 figure with 2 Anglo-Indians is outdated.

new.s: Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides for raising Andhra Pradesh Assembly seats from 175 to:
new.x: Section 26 raises AP seats from 175 to 225 (Telangana 119 to 153), subject to Article 170.

new.s: How many Lok Sabha seats in Telangana are reserved for Scheduled Tribes?
new.x: Telangana has 2 ST seats (Adilabad, Mahabubabad) and 3 SC seats; Andhra Pradesh has 1 ST seat (Araku).

new.s: Under Article 333, the Governor could nominate how many Anglo-Indian members to a State Assembly?
new.x: Article 333 allowed the Governor to nominate one Anglo-Indian; Article 331 allowed two to the Lok Sabha. Both ended with the 104th Amendment.

new.s: Under Section 81 of the RPA, 1951, an election petition must be filed within how many days of the returned candidate's election?
new.x: Section 81 sets a 45-day limit for filing an election petition.

new.s: Election petitions under the RPA, 1951 are tried by the:
new.x: Under Section 80A, election petitions are tried by the High Court, with appeal to the Supreme Court.

new.s: The rule that no election can be called in question except by an election petition is in which Section of the RPA, 1951?
new.x: Section 80 bars questioning an election except by petition; Section 81 is the 45-day limit.

new.s: How many recognised national parties were there in 2025?
new.x: In 2025 there were six national parties: BJP, INC, BSP, CPI(M), AAP and NPP.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised national party (2025)?
new.x: TMC, NCP and CPI lost national status; the six national parties are BJP, INC, BSP, CPI(M), AAP and NPP.

new.s: The Model Code of Conduct is best described as:
o: Election Commission guidelines not enacted by Parliament
new.x: The MCC is a set of ECI guidelines, not a statute; its authority comes from Article 324.

new.s: In which case was it held that the Model Code of Conduct comes into force from the announcement of the election schedule?
o: Kuldip Nayar v Union of India
Harbans Singh Jalal v Union of India
new.x: Harbans Singh Jalal v UoI (1997, Punjab and Haryana HC) held the MCC applies from the announcement of the schedule.

new.s: If NOTA receives the highest number of votes in a constituency:
o: The candidate with the most votes is still declared elected
The Election Commission nominates a member
new.x: NOTA is symbolic: even if it gets the most votes, the top candidate wins and there is no fresh poll.

new.s: Indelible election ink is applied on the voter's:
new.x: Indelible ink, made by Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd, is applied on the left forefinger.

new.s: The cVIGIL app of the Election Commission lets citizens:
o: Report Model Code violations with geo-tagged photos or videos
Help elderly voters in Jammu and Kashmir
new.x: cVIGIL reports MCC violations, with action within 100 minutes; NETA rates representatives, Sahulat helps J&K elderly voters and Saksham serves voters with disabilities.

new.s: The first State to provide Braille-enabled ballots at all polling booths was:
new.x: Meghalaya was the first State with Braille-enabled ballots at all booths (APPSC 2018).

new.s: Under SVEEP, the voter education programme of 2009, the Election Commission partnered with:
new.x: The ECI partnered Indian Railways under SVEEP for voter awareness (APPSC 2019).

new.s: Section 126A of the RPA, 1951 bars exit polls from the start of polling in the first phase till:
o: Half an hour after the last phase closes
48 hours before the close of poll
One hour after the first phase closes
new.x: Section 126A bars exit polls until half an hour after the last phase; the 48-hour bar under Section 126 is for opinion polls.

new.s: How many general elections to the Lok Sabha have been held so far, with the 2024 election included?
new.x: Eighteen general elections have been held; the 18th Lok Sabha was elected in 2024.

new.s: Under Section 15 of the RPA, 1951, the notification for a State Assembly general election is issued by the:
new.x: The Governor notifies Assembly polls (Section 15) and the President Lok Sabha polls (Section 14); the ECI never issues the notification.

new.s: Which officer conducts the poll in a constituency and declares the result?
new.x: The Returning Officer conducts the poll and declares the result; the DEO, usually the Collector, receives expense accounts.

new.s: The preparation of electoral rolls is dealt with in the:
new.x: RPA 1950 covers the pre-election framework including electoral rolls; RPA 1951 covers actual conduct of elections.

new.s: Article 325 of the Constitution provides for:
o: Adult suffrage for Lok Sabha and Assemblies
One general electoral roll for every territorial constituency
A bar on courts in electoral matters
new.x: Article 325 provides one general electoral roll per constituency with no exclusion on religion, race, caste or sex.

new.s: Articles 324 to 329 on elections are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
new.x: Part XV (Articles 324-329) deals with elections.

new.s: Which of the following was a member of the Ram Nath Kovind High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections?
new.x: Members included Amit Shah, Ghulam Nabi Azad, N.K. Singh, Subhash C. Kashyap, Harish Salve and Sanjay Kothari.

new.s: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 proposes to insert Article:
new.x: The Bill inserts Article 82A and amends Articles 83, 172 and 327.

new.s: In December 2024 the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill was referred to a:
new.x: The Bill was sent to a JPC in December 2024, which was still examining it in February 2026.

new.s: The current election expenditure limit for an Assembly candidate in a larger State is:
new.x: Assembly candidates in larger States may spend ₹40 lakh (earlier ₹28 lakh); ₹95 lakh is the Lok Sabha limit.

new.s: The expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in a smaller State or UT is:
new.x: Smaller States/UTs have a Lok Sabha limit of ₹75 lakh (earlier ₹54 lakh).

new.s: Candidate expenditure limits are prescribed under Rule 90 of the:
new.x: Limits are fixed under Rule 90, Conduct of Election Rules 1961, raised by the 2022 Amendment Rules.

new.s: In Public Interest Foundation v Union of India (2018), on disqualifying candidates once charges are framed, the Supreme Court:
o: Made it a ground under Section 8
Directed the ECI to bar such candidates
new.x: The five-judge bench did not disqualify on framing of charges and left it to Parliament, but required parties to publish criminal records.

new.s: In PUCL v Union of India (2003), the Supreme Court struck down which Section of the RPA, 1951?
new.x: PUCL (2003) upheld the voter's right to know under Article 19(1)(a) and struck down Section 33B.

new.s: Lily Thomas v Union of India (2013) struck down which provision of the RPA, 1951?
new.x: Lily Thomas struck down Section 8(4), the three-month appeal buffer, making disqualification immediate on conviction.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about State funding of elections:
1. Germany, Sweden, Japan and Canada practise it.
2. Under full State funding, private donations are banned.
3. The Indrajit Gupta Committee's recommendation was adopted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Indrajit Gupta Committee's recommendation of partial funding was not adopted.

new.s: The ban on liquor sale for 48 hours before a poll, added in 1996, is in which Section of the RPA, 1951?
new.x: Section 135C bans liquor; 135B gives a paid holiday and 151A requires by-polls within 6 months.

new.s: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly elections of which of the following States?
new.x: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly polls of Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi.

new.s: The first use of an EVM in India, on 19 May 1982, was in which State?
new.x: EVMs were first used at 70-Parur in Kerala in 1982; Goa (1999) was the first whole-State poll.

new.s: An M3 EVM control unit can handle up to how many candidates, including NOTA?
new.x: One M3 control unit takes 24 ballot units, i.e. 384 candidates including NOTA; the M2 took 64.

new.s: A VVPAT slip is visible to the voter through a window for:
new.x: The VVPAT slip is shown for 7 seconds and is not handed to the voter.

new.s: The 2004 election to the 14th Lok Sabha was the first:
o: National election held entirely on EVMs
new.x: 2004 was the first all-EVM national election; VVPAT and NOTA came in 2013.

new.s: A Remote EVM (RVM) can handle up to how many constituencies from one remote polling station?
new.x: The RVM, for domestic migrants, can cover up to 72 constituencies from one remote station.

new.s: Under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023, who was dropped from the selection panel?
new.x: The 2023 Act panel is the PM, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM and the LoP; the CJI was dropped.

new.s: The Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms (1974-75) was set up by:
new.x: The Tarkunde Committee was set up by JP; it proposed a 3-member ECI and voting age 18.

new.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission, which reported on 'Ethics in Governance', was chaired by:
new.x: The 2nd ARC (2007-09) under Veerappa Moily recommended partial State funding.

new.s: Under Section 34 of the RPA, 1951, the security deposit for a general-category Assembly candidate is:
new.x: The deposit is ₹10,000 for Assembly and ₹25,000 for Lok Sabha; SC/ST candidates pay half.

new.s: Electoral bonds could be bought by:
o: A citizen of India or a body incorporated in India
Only companies listed on a stock exchange
new.x: Bonds could be bought by a citizen of India or a body incorporated in India, alone or jointly.

new.s: The Electoral Bond Scheme was notified on:
new.x: The scheme was notified on 2 January 2018 and struck down on 15 February 2024.

new.s: The 2024 electoral bonds verdict in ADR v Union of India was delivered by:
new.x: A five-judge bench unanimously held the scheme unconstitutional.

new.s:
Arrange the following parties in chronological order of formation:
1. Swatantra Party
2. Bharatiya Janata Party
3. Telugu Desam Party
4. Bahujan Samaj Party
The Telugu Desam Party was formed in:
new.x: The TDP was formed by NTR in 1982, between the BJP (1980) and the BSP (1984).

new.s: Which of the following parties was formed earliest?
new.x: Forward Bloc (1939) came before the DMK (1949), Jana Sangh (1951) and Swatantra (1959).

new.s: Which of the following parties was formed after the Janata Dal (1988)?
new.x: The Samajwadi Party was formed in 1992; the BSP (1984), TDP (1982) and BJP (1980) came earlier.

new.s: The Swatantra Party (1959) was founded by:
new.x: Rajagopalachari founded Swatantra; Narendra Dev, JP and Lohia were Socialist Party leaders.

new.s: The Samajwadi Party was founded in 1992 at:
new.x: Mulayam Singh Yadav founded the SP at Lucknow on 4 October 1992.

new.s: The DMK was founded in 1949 by:
new.x: C.N. Annadurai founded the DMK in 1949, out of Periyar's Dravidar Kazhagam.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about political parties:
1. The Samajwadi Party is a recognised national party.
2. The Republican Party of India was formed after Dr B.R. Ambedkar's death.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Only statement 2 is correct: the RPI was planned by Ambedkar and formed after his death; the SP is not a national party.

new.s: Who was elected BJP national president unopposed on 20 January 2026?
new.x: Nitin Nabin, aged 45, succeeded J.P. Nadda as the youngest BJP national president.

new.s: Mallikarjun Kharge has been president of the Indian National Congress since:
new.x: Kharge became INC president in October 2022, the first non-Gandhi in 24 years.

new.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao is associated with the:
new.x: Harisarvottama Rao led the Andhra Swaraj Party (1934); Madduri Annapurnayya was Forward Bloc and Sundarayya the Andhra Communist Party.

new.s: The Congress for Democracy (1977) was formed by:
new.x: Jagjivan Ram, with H.N. Bahuguna and Nandini Satpathy, formed the Congress for Democracy in 1977.

new.s: The phase of one-party dominance, the 'Congress system', covers:
new.x: Congress dominance ran 1952-77; 1977-89 saw the first alternation and 1989-2014 the coalition era.

new.s: The first non-Congress government at the Centre (1977) was headed by:
new.x: The Janata government of 1977 under Morarji Desai was the first non-Congress and first coalition government.

new.s: The Kamaraj Plan was introduced in:
new.x: Under the Kamaraj Plan (1963) senior Congress ministers resigned to work for the party.

new.s: A party can be recognised as a State party on vote share alone if it secures:
new.x: The vote-only threshold for State party status is 8%, not 10%.

new.s: Registered unrecognised parties and independents contest elections on:
new.x: Recognised parties get reserved symbols; RUPPs and independents get free symbols (184 in May 2025).

new.s: Under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951, a party must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to the principles of:
new.x: A party applying under Section 29A pledges allegiance to the Constitution, socialism, secularism, democracy and national integrity.

new.s: Donations above ₹2,000 to a political party must be made:
o: In cash through the party treasurer
In cash deposited with the ECI
new.x: Donations above ₹2,000 may be made only by cheque or bank transfer; ₹20,000 is the disclosure threshold.
